about.label: About
about.summary: I make games, prototypes, and weird little systems that somehow start as "this should be quick" and end with me happily deep in architecture, tools, and backend logic.
body: I have been working with Unity for more than a decade, which is long enough to have made a lot of things, broken a lot of things, and become suspicious whenever someone says a feature is just a simple little addition.

Over the years I have gone from self-directed experimentation and small projects into building more reusable gameplay systems, better workflows, and tools that help teams move faster without setting the whole project on fire.

Most of my work lives in the space between programming and design. I like solving the practical problems that make games feel better to build and better to play, whether that is gameplay architecture, iteration speed, multiplayer logic, or backend systems that do their job quietly in the background.
I have worked across personal projects, team projects, jam games, and shipped releases, and I tend to gravitate toward the technical glue that holds everything together.
I have also recently started my Advanced Diploma in Game Design, so alongside building games professionally and independently, I am still actively sharpening the design side of my work too.

clusters.label: Gameplay Programming
clusters.summary: Builds responsive, state-driven gameplay with clear ownership, predictable transitions, and tuning surfaces that support rapid designer iteration. Treats input, animation, camera, audio and feedback as one player-facing system while keeping the implementation debuggable enough to survive production.

clusters.label: Unity & C#
clusters.summary: More than a decade of practical Unity experience, focused on maintainable C#, dependable component boundaries, and workflows that remain understandable as projects grow.

clusters.label: Systems Design
clusters.summary: Turns design goals into readable mechanics, progression and player feedback, balancing technical constraints against clarity, pacing and long-term engagement.

clusters.label: Tools & Workflow
clusters.summary: Creates focused tools and diagnostics that shorten iteration loops, expose useful data, and let designers spend more time improving the game.

clusters.label: Production & Teamwork
clusters.summary: Scopes work honestly, communicates trade-offs early, and delivers readable systems that teammates can review, extend and confidently take ownership of.

clusters.label: Multiplayer & Backend
clusters.summary: Approaches networking from a client-server mindset, with server-authoritative state, validated inputs, predictable failure handling and player-facing responsiveness.

clusters.label: Platforms & Performance
clusters.summary: Treats performance as a design constraint: protecting frame time, memory and stability while adapting features to the realities of each target platform.
